source_text: Illud eminentius: fecit Deus hominem, ad imaginem Dei fecit eum — quod neque de caelo neque de terra neque de sole dictum. Hunc ad imaginem non corporalem intelligimus. Corpus plasmatus est de limo; qui ad imaginem factus est, interior homo est, invisibilis, incorporalis, incorruptus, immortalis. Qui corporeum putat ad imaginem, Deum corporeum inducit — impium. Coelum mihi sedes non pedum extensionem, sed in caelestium conversatione requiem Dei significat.
pass_a_gloss: That more-eminent: made God human, to image of-God made him — which neither about heaven nor about earth nor about sun said. This to image not bodily we-understand. Body molded is from mud; who to image made is, interior human is, invisible, bodiless, incorrupt, immortal. Who bodily thinks to image, God bodily introduces — impious. Heaven to-me throne not of-feet extension, but in of-heavenly-ones citizenship rest of-God signifies.
pass_b_english: More exalted still: [[God made humankind; in the image of God he made them >> Bible:Genesis 1:27]] — said neither of heaven nor of earth nor of the sun. We do not take this “in the image” as bodily. The body was [[molded from the mud of the earth >> Bible:Genesis 2:7]]; the one made in the image is our interior human — invisible, bodiless, incorrupt, immortal. To think the bodily is in the image is to invent a bodily God — impious. [[Heaven is my throne >> Bible:Isaiah 66:1]] does not mean stretched feet, but God’s rest in the citizenship of those whose [[commonwealth is in heaven >> Bible:Philippians 3:20]].
